theory: Distinguish an underlying continuous measurement from its rounded recorded random variable, which is discrete. Infinitely many possible values alone do not imply zero probability at every point; attribute this property to the continuous distribution and zero-width area. The illustrated function is not a normalized density, and its boundary lines do not meet the curve. Replace the claim that probability is only meaningful over an interval with the precise statement that individual values have probability $0$.
